Propose exactly 1 DISTINCT, implementable idea for improving the item semantic IDs that a generative recommender consumes. You are one of 5 independent ideation agents: aim for a different part of the design space than the others, and do not copy an existing mechanism in the repository.
THE RESEARCH OBJECTIVE:
Discover new mechanisms in which TRAINING-ONLY user behaviour and HYPERBOLIC geometry are computationally coupled to improve the RQ-VAE Semantic IDs used by a generative next-item recommender, with the real target of Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065.
THE SCOPE CONTRACT (a proposal that misses it is sent back, not scored):
A proposal is IN SCOPE only when all of this holds:
  1. BEHAVIOUR: it names one training-only behaviour signal (directed item transitions, user-interest branching, sequential co-consumption, popularity-adjusted graph neighbours, behaviour-conditioned assignment weights, ...) and says how it is computed.
  2. HYPERBOLIC GEOMETRY: it names an explicit curved operation (trainable or fixed negative curvature, Poincare or Lorentz distance, exp/log maps, geodesic scoring, curved residual, curved quantization, curved regularization) and where in training or quantization it acts.
  3. REAL COUPLING: one connected computational pathway uses both, so that removing either changes the core computation. A behaviour suffix on an unchanged Euclidean quantizer, a standalone hyperbolic loss beside an unrelated behaviour loss, a geometry name without geometric computation, or inherited unused hyperbolic code do NOT qualify.
  4. TESTABLE EFFECT: it states what should observably change (SID assignment, gradient or parameter update, prefix behaviour predictability, or Stage3 Recall) and names the behaviour-off, geometry-off/Euclidean and both-on comparisons. The three switches must be part of the mechanism, so that the coupling can be shown to be real, but the round RUNS no ablation arm: each candidate is trained once.
  5. MINIMAL SPECIFICATION: equations or pseudocode, inputs and outputs, numerical safeguards and the training cost. No proof and no paper section are required.
SID quality (ER, prefix counts, collisions) is NOT a scope criterion and NOT an admission rule.

EXPERIMENT POLICY (binding on every proposal, implementation and review):
  - ONE candidate, ONE training run, on the frozen budget (3000 Stage 2 epochs on four cards, the frozen Stage 3 protocol, no early stopping).
  - NO ablation experiments: the behaviour-off, geometry-off and both-on switches must EXIST in the code and must be correct, but no arm is trained with them switched off.
  - NO tuning experiments: no sweep over the coupling weight, the clip bound, the temperature, the usage weight or any other constant. A constant that enters the mechanism has to be DERIVED (a scale-relative bound, a measured quantity, a documented default), not chosen by trying values.
  - NO multi-seed experiments: a candidate is not repeated with other seeds, so a single run decides it and the seed noise is part of the uncertainty.
  - The behavioural diagnostics (coherence, adjacency, transfer predictability) are recorded, never used as an admission gate; Stage 3 test_recall@10 is the judgement.
  - A proposal that needs an ablation, a sweep or a seed repetition to make its case is out of programme: it has to make the case with one run.
Explore materially different coupling positions, for example: behaviour-weighted curved assignment or Sinkhorn; behaviour hierarchy in a negatively curved latent or quantizer; behaviour-directed curved residual or transition optimization. These are examples, not a fixed list.

A SECOND exploration of the behaviour-graph curvature, aimed at the failure the FIRST one measured. The first round (round_20261102_031529_470) selected CURVALLOC-LORENTZ-RQ: the standardised Ollivier curvature of the training behaviour quotient graph was spent on each level's curvature c_l and code radius rho_l inside the RQ-VAE's assignment. It ran end to end and it FAILED: the mechanism did act -- the measured profile kappa_hat = [0.00, -8.96, -25.55] gave delta = [0.702, 0.298, -1.000] and therefore curvature = [0.496, 0.743, 2.718] and code radius = [0.0381, 0.0312, 0.0163], which is the direction the correlation analysis favours (a flatter coarse level, a more curved fine level) -- but the code radius it spent was so small that the codebook's own resolution collapsed: the exported SID had 2 first-level codes, 13 second-level prefixes and 56 three-token SIDs (the inherited baseline TIGER_BRad-RQ had 12/60/170, the frozen baseline 247/7414/20223), the collision rate was 0.998, the valid L1 positive and negative hit rates were 0.982 and 0.980 (the first token carries no information), and Stage3 test_recall@10 was 0.041888, BELOW the 0.0446 of the arm it inherited and 36% below the 0.065 target. The lesson, measured and not assumed: the standardised curvature profile tracks which SID tables turn out well (Spearman -0.20 for the level-1 minus level-3 deviation over 115 mechanism families) but spending it on the geometry trades the codebook's resolution away, and resolution is what the recall needs. THIS ROUND's question: can the behaviour-graph curvature be used WITHOUT spending resolution? Routes worth considering, each of which must compute the curvature from the TRAINING split only, keep it STANDARDISED against a size-preserving member-shuffle null (the raw curvature is unrelated to the recall: Spearman +0.03, p=0.65, because the level sizes differ), and couple it to the curved geometry in ONE connected computational path so that removing either the behaviour term or the geometry changes the assignment: (a) the curvature enters as a CONSTRAINT ON THE ASSIGNMENT or a loss on the realised geometry, rather than as the space's radius, so the codebook's radius is untouched; (b) the curvature profile is enforced on the ITEM side (the encoder's geometry) while the codes keep their own scale; (c) a per-code or per-region curvature field (each code's own chart curvature) with the global radius left alone; (d) the profile chooses BETWEEN existing mechanisms or assignment rules rather than rescaling anything. Every proposal must state explicitly how its resolution is protected -- the measured numbers to beat are the frozen baseline's 247/7414/20223 and its Stage3 test_recall@10 of 0.055537, and a proposal that trades resolution for curvature is a known failure, not a candidate. The three switches (behaviour off, geometry off/Euclidean, both on) must be part of the mechanism, the curvature measurement must carry no gradient (it is a schedule or a penalty, not a backpropagated quantity), and the mechanism must run under the four-rank recipe without a collective that only rank 0 executes while the other ranks wait in a broadcast (the first round lost three launches to exactly that: a CPU broadcast, an oversized transport support, and a rank-0 export that deadlocked against the other ranks' broadcast).
